Age of first production of words

Source: R/data.R
first_words.Rd

Parents of 60 children acquiring European Portuguese report each month, from 10 to 24 months, whether their child says each of 40 words. For each child and word, the data give the age at which the child first said the word, or 24 months if the child had not said it by the end of the study (a censored observation). Frequent words and nouns are learned earlier. For survival analysis.

Usage

first_words

Format

A tibble with 2400 rows and 6 columns:

child

Child ID, C01 to C60.

word

Word ID, w01 to w40.

category

"noun", "verb" or "other".

log_freq

log10 frequency of the word in child-directed speech.

age

Age in months at first production, or 24 if censored.

produced

1 if the child said the word by 24 months, 0 if censored.

Source

data-raw/first_words.R

Details

True model: a discrete-time hazard. In each month from 10 to 24 the probability of first saying a word is plogis(-5.2 + 0.28 * (age - 10) + 0.6 * (log_freq - 2) + category + c0 + w0), with category effects 0.5 (noun), -0.3 (verb) and -0.6 (other), by-child effects c0 (SD 0.6) and by-word effects w0 (SD 0.4). About 37% of observations are censored.

Examples

head(first_words)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 6
#>   child word  category log_freq   age produced
#>   <fct> <fct> <fct>       <dbl> <int>    <int>
#> 1 C01   w01   noun         1.3     24        0
#> 2 C01   w02   noun         1.16    24        0
#> 3 C01   w03   noun         1.31    21        1
#> 4 C01   w04   noun         3.39    13        1
#> 5 C01   w05   noun         2.91    24        0
#> 6 C01   w06   noun         2.14    23        1
